clue.text: Perhaps workers take heart from beautiful women

indicators.note: taking the heart from a word removes its central letters, here the middle pair

parts.note: belles are beautiful women

explanation.surface: Labourers lift their spirits by looking at attractive women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take heart from' removes LL, the middle pair of BELLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker bees are the labouring caste of a hive, so the insects are an example of workers, flagged by 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Banish text spelt without using cases

indicators.note: cases are the outer letters, so each word is taken without its first and last

explanation.surface: Ban text written without capital letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' suggests upper and lower case, but here it means the outside letters of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive out or exile someone is to banish them.

clue.text: Distribute fantasy news made for nothing

indicators.note: to distribute is to spread things out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Spread fake news invented out of thin air.
explanation.walkthrough: A British slang phrase, often shortened to SFA, meaning nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial British phrase meaning nothing whatsoever, originally naval slang.

clue.text: Perverted Right Honourable member in game involving rubber

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Rt Hon is the abbreviation of Right Honourable, the title of a Privy Counsellor

explanation.surface: A corrupt MP is caught up in some game featuring rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perverted' rearranges RTHON. A rubber is a match in bridge, played by four partners named by compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, scored in rubbers, the four seated players are called after compass points, and this one partners South.

clue.text: Knotty problem with our land

indicators.note: a problem with letters means they are in difficulty, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knotty issue concerning our country.
explanation.definitionFit: Having small lumps or nodes, like knots in wood, means knotty.

clue.text: He had a hand in 24 and 8 down

definitions.text: He had a hand in 24 and 8 down

parts.words: He had a hand in 24 and 8 down
parts.note: the puppeteer Hull worked the bird Emu (24 down) with his arm inside it, and his first name sits within the letters of 8 down

explanation.walkthrough: 24 down is EMU, the puppet worked by the British entertainer Hull with his hand inside it; 8 down, ELECTRODE, contains the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The entertainer Hull, famous for his violent puppet emu, had this first name, which is also a word inside the conductor.

clue.text: One entertaining East German Nazi guards

indicators.note: guards means surrounds to protect, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was a leading Nazi
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: An East German is entertained under watch by Nazi guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like a person, but it is the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who receives and entertains guests is one entertaining.

clue.text: Cooker draining current from main

indicators.note: draining something empties it out, so a letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: main means chief, principal
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A cooker drawing electricity from the mains supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooker' reads as the appliance, but it is the person who cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who prepares meals in a kitchen is literally one who cooks.

clue.text: A rare condition's breached this barrier method

indicators.note: breached means broken through, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A barrier contraceptive that failed because of a rare condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrier method' looks like contraception, but means a quarantine line round an infected area.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarded line preventing anyone leaving an infected area, used to stop disease spreading.

clue.text: Conductor's chosen right verse

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president-elect
an ode is a poem, a piece of verse

explanation.surface: An orchestra conductor has picked the right poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests an orchestra; here it conducts electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal through which electric current enters or leaves conducts electricity.

clue.text: First-class Latin dons pass papers

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so one piece wears the other and holds it inside

parts.note: to pass time is to spend it
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Top-flight Oxbridge Latin tutors hand round documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university tutors but is a verb: SPEND puts on L.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives of high praise meaning excellent or superb in quality.

clue.text: Died after legless doctor heaved

indicators.note: after places the letter for died at the end
leg side in cricket is also called the on side, so removing the letters for leg cuts them out

parts.note: a surgeon is a kind of doctor

explanation.surface: Someone died after a drunk doctor retched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legless' (British slang for very drunk) removes ON, cricket's other name for the leg side, from SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a sea or crowd rising and swelling with a strong upward movement.

clue.text: Smallest member let into toilet that's out of order

indicators.note: something out of order is jumbled, so these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken toilet that the smallest club member is allowed into.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth digit of the foot is the smallest limb-part, and a member here means a body part.

clue.text: Loveless couple go off meaningless talk

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, so loveless drops that letter

parts.note: a couple is two
eggs go off when they addle, turn rotten

explanation.surface: A couple whose love has gone sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly, trivial chatter without sense is meaningless talk, nonsense.

clue.text: Labour leader abandons reluctant pledge

indicators.note: abandons means leaves behind, so this letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: loath means unwilling or reluctant

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Labour Party leader backs out of a promise he was unwilling to make.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn promise or sworn vow is a pledge.

clue.text: Zebra skin stocked by dodgy Arab shop

indicators.note: stocked by means held as stock inside, so one piece sits within the other
dodgy means unreliable, so these letters are scrambled
the skin of a word is its outer layer, first and last letters

explanation.surface: Zebra hides sold by a shady Arab trader in a market shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges ARAB to BAAR; 'skin' gives ZA from Zebra.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is a market or a shop selling assorted goods, especially in the Middle East.

clue.text: Instrument for simulating the production of heavy metal

definitions.text: Instrument for simulating the production of heavy metal

parts.words: Instrument for simulating the production of heavy metal
parts.note: heavy metal suggests lead or uranium, but the music is mimed on an imaginary strummed instrument

explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' suggests smelting; it is the rock music genre, and the instrument is an imaginary one played in mime.
explanation.definitionFit: Fans mimicking rock guitarists strum an invisible instrument to fake playing heavy metal.

clue.text: One makes ratings broadcast SOS, close to disaster on high seas

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread and rearranged

parts.words: SOS, close to disaster on high seas
parts.note: the fodder is SOS as written, the last letter of disaster (its close), and seas as written, which sits on top of them

explanation.surface: Sailors send a distress call as disaster looms on the open ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges SOS, R (the close of 'disaster') and SEAS. 'Ratings' looks like naval sailors, but means assessments.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who evaluates property for tax or rates, or grades performance, assigns ratings.

clue.text: Novel published on account of being in digital format

indicators.note: being in means placed inside, so these pieces sit within the other

parts.note: CD is a compact disc, a digital format
a newspaper ran a story when it published it
for can mean because of, on account of

explanation.surface: A novel was released only as a digital edition.
explanation.walkthrough: One of Elizabeth Gaskell's novels, set in a small English town; her name is in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a book by Elizabeth Gaskell, a work of fiction from the 1850s.

clue.text: Top policeman journalists treat harshly

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: A senior police officer is harsh with reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like senior rank, but is a verb meaning cut the head off.
explanation.definitionFit: To persecute or keep down by cruel use of power is to treat harshly.

clue.text: Soundly beat target in game after suspension

indicators.note: soundly means by sound, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to beat an opponent is to conquer them

explanation.surface: Thoroughly defeat a target in a game after it was put on hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but signals a homophone. Conkers is a British children's game: a horse chestnut hung on a string is swung at the opponent's.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game of conkers each chestnut dangles on a string and is the target of the other player's swing.

clue.text: Big cat trainer for Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the sounds of words, so the two syllables of this word trade sounds

parts.note: a trainer of pupils is a teacher, a word whose first syllable is the sound tea
the same word for a trainer of pupils, whose second syllable is the sound cher

explanation.surface: A wild cat's handler, as Spooner might say.
explanation.walkthrough: A Spoonerism within one word: TEA-CHER swaps its sounds to CHEE-TAH.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest land animal is a large spotted wild feline, a big cat.

clue.text: One objection about means of producing notes

indicators.note: about means turned round, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: one is the article a
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A single objection concerning a way of printing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests banknotes, but here they are musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: This large brass instrument produces low musical notes.

clue.text: Put forward current borders of England

parts.note: present means current, existing now

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A proposal concerning the present frontiers of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer or submit something for consideration is to put it forward.

clue.text: Compulsion to remove university gown

indicators.note: to remove means to take away, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: duress is compulsion by threats

explanation.surface: Forced to take off one's academic gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's garment, or a formal robe, is a gown.

clue.text: Essential character of Spare Rib is relaxed

indicators.note: the essential character of a word is its central letter, at its heart

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: The core spirit of the feminist magazine Spare Rib is laid-back.
explanation.walkthrough: Spare Rib was a British feminist magazine; 'Essential character of' takes A, the middle letter of 'Spare'.
explanation.definitionFit: A military command and an idiom both meaning comfortable and free from tension.

clue.text: Required prescription for ecstasy?

parts.note: E is the drug ecstasy; the pair of letters EN with its tail cut off leaves this single letter

explanation.surface: A doctor's script is needed for the drug ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as EN TAILED: the letters EN with the tail removed leave E, the usual abbreviation for ecstasy. So the answer is a recipe for producing ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: If something necessarily involves another thing, that thing is required by it.

clue.text: Bird releasing doctor's grip on object

indicators.note: releasing its grip means letting go of, so these letters are removed

parts.note: to demur is to object
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A bird gets free of a vet's grip on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a noun but is the verb, to raise an objection; 'releasing' lets go of the doctor's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless Australian bird is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Government expert on cycling skills

indicators.note: cycling means moving letters round from one end to the other

parts.note: a tsar is a government-appointed expert, such as a drugs tsar

explanation.surface: A ministerial adviser on cycling skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on cycling' moves TS from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafts or techniques that need practice are known as skills, as in the arts of war.

clue.text: Point out when it's quiet outside

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Point out when things have gone quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point out' looks like one verb; 'Point' is the definition, a compass point. Gaskell's North and South is the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Start to endow higher education institution instead

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: Fund a university as an alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean otherwise or as an alternative, as in 'or else'.
